subsystems.name: Computational lattice
subsystems.role: the planet's matter rearranged into a three-dimensional array of logic and memory elements — often called computronium.

subsystems.name: Interconnect
subsystems.role: moves data between elements while keeping every path short, because signals cannot travel faster than light.

subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: supplies the energy for computation without needing a nearby star.
parts: internal fusion or residual thermal energy

subsystems.name: Thermal system
subsystems.role: carries waste heat from the interior to the outer surface and radiates it to space.

subsystems.name: Control and error correction
subsystems.role: keeps a machine of planetary scale coherent and fault-tolerant.

subsystems.name: Self-maintenance
subsystems.role: repairs and replaces degraded elements without outside help.

buildSteps.title: Select and survey a gas giant
buildSteps.detail: Mass, composition and available energy set the ceiling on how much computation the object can ever do.

buildSteps.title: Disassemble the planet
buildSteps.detail: Its hydrogen and helium are separated and its heavier elements extracted, rather than left as a ball of gas.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture computronium
buildSteps.detail: Matter is rebuilt into atomically precise logic and memory elements — this step assumes molecular manufacturing that does not yet exist.

buildSteps.title: Assemble in three dimensions
buildSteps.detail: Elements are packed into nested shells or a lattice, with the layout chosen to keep signal delays short and uniform.

buildSteps.title: Install power and cooling
buildSteps.detail: Coolant loops and heat pumps move waste heat outward to a large radiating surface.

buildSteps.title: Bring it online gradually
buildSteps.detail: The machine boots in sections, with error correction and self-test at each level before the next is activated.

buildSteps.title: Run near the thermodynamic limit
buildSteps.detail: Computation is made as reversible as possible to cut heat generation, since every bit erased costs at least about 3×10⁻²¹ joules at room temperature.

buildSteps.title: Operate and repair
buildSteps.detail: Faulty regions are rebuilt in place from local material over very long timescales.

prerequisites.why: rebuilding planetary mass into working logic elements demands assembly at the atomic scale at enormous throughput.

prerequisites.tech: Reversible computing near the Landauer limit
prerequisites.why: only near-reversible operation keeps heat output low enough for a body this size; today's chips are many orders of magnitude less efficient.
long internal links must carry signals with minimal loss and minimal heating.
radiated power grows with surface area and the fourth power of temperature, so cooling — not fabrication — caps the design.
the machine needs a supply that does not depend on capturing sunlight from outside.

pathway.milestone: theoretical work on the physical limits of computing — Landauer's principle, Bremermann's limit and the Bekenstein bound
pathway.unlocks: a clear ceiling on what any given mass and temperature can compute.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations of reversible logic and molecular-scale devices
pathway.unlocks: evidence that computation far below today's energy cost per operation is possible.

pathway.milestone: self-replicating or self-assembling manufacturing at scale
pathway.unlocks: construction of very large structures without vast human labour.

pathway.milestone: megastructures assembled in space from non-terrestrial material
pathway.unlocks: the industrial base from which a planet-mass computer could in principle be built.
